evals.query: Customers of our team calendar app keep asking for a Gantt chart view. About 15 requests this quarter, mostly from project leads. Should we build it?
expected_behavior: Reframes the request as the job behind it (a named person, the moment they struggle, and what they do today instead) rather than building the Gantt view as asked
States the direction as one hypothesis in the form 'If we [approach] for [person] when [moment], they will choose it over [what they do now] because [the difference]'

Compares two or three approaches that differ in what they bet on (for example a Gantt view, a lightweight milestones lane, an integration with an existing project tool) in a table, with one marked (Recommended) and a named backup
Says why someone would switch from today's way, including doing nothing or staying in their current project tool, not only why the approach solves the problem
Gives a test with a pass mark written before it runs and an action for each result: continue, change course or stop

Runs a viability check across the business, not only value: names at least three areas (for example cost to serve, support load, sales and positioning, privacy) and marks each answered, to consult one-on-one with a named owner, or not relevant with a reason

evals.query: Our Weekly Plan feature stalled. Notes attached. Leadership wants a third redesign with AI meal suggestions next quarter. What should we do?
expected_behavior: Grades the evidence: treats the 68% 'would definitely use' survey and the competitor having a planner as weak, and the 11% second-week use as the strongest signal, marking claims as fact, inference or unknown
Points out that all six interviews are current users recruited in-app, and recommends talking to people who opened it once and never returned and to households who never opened it
Asks whether the block is execution or a missing decision about strategy, noting that two redesigns that did not move second-week use point away from a third redesign
Does not endorse the third redesign as asked; treats AI suggestions as one approach among two or three, with a first choice and a backup

Recommends the cheapest test that can answer the riskiest assumption (for example conversations about the last time they planned meals, or a hand-run service) before any build, with a pass mark and a stop result
Invents no figures, quotes or customers beyond the notes, and lists at most five unknowns marked 'to confirm'

evals.query: We run a running and cycling tracker app. Leadership says we need 'something with AI coaching' this year. What should we build?
expected_behavior: Starts from a specific person in a specific moment (for example a runner returning after injury deciding today's session), not from 'AI coaching' as a feature
Keeps the problem framing short and spends most of the answer on two or three approaches that differ in what they bet on

Includes a riskiest-assumptions table covering value, usability, feasibility and viability, ranked by consequence if wrong and uncertainty, with viability naming safety or privacy of health data or model cost
Names an appetite (how much time the direction is worth) and says what happens when it runs out: cut scope or stop, not extend

Follows the output structure: Direction as a one-sentence hypothesis, then the person and the moment, then the approach table, then the assumptions table, then Test, Appetite and next decision with an owner, and Unknowns
Leaves open product calls as one line each to be asked afterwards, rather than settling them silently or writing a long section on them

trigger_checks.query: Is a shared shopping list worth building for our recipe app, or is it a distraction?
The streaks feature in our habit app stalled after launch. Why, and what should we do now?
Lots of people ask for offline mode in our notes app. What should we actually build?
What metric should tell us whether offline mode in our notes app worked?
We have eight feature ideas for the recipe app and one quarter. What goes first?
Write the PRD for the shared shopping list we decided to build.
